The related noun-case pattern also applies in inanimate accusative contexts, with the appropriate noun form. Other sentence cases require numeral declension as well as noun declension. A count ending in one outside the teen exception uses a nominative singular noun in the shown basic phrases. один час — один час. два часа — два часа.
A count ending in two, three or four outside the teen exception uses a genitive singular noun in the basic construction. This is a grammatical singular form even though the count is greater than one.
Counts ending in zero or five through nine use genitive plural in the basic construction. The teen exception also uses genitive plural. Ten and sixteen therefore fit this pattern. пять часов — пять часов. двадцать один час — двадцать один час.
For a compound count, inspect the last two digits first. If they are 11, 12, 13 or 14, use genitive plural for the counted noun in the basic construction. Otherwise, the final digit selects the pattern: one, two-through-four, or zero/five-through-nine. Compare 21 and 22: their final digits select different noun cases; being larger than five is not enough to choose genitive plural. двадцать два часа — двадцать два часа. две девушки — two girls.

The retained examples are long past passive forms with adjective-type endings. In the shown сде́ланный and напи́санный forms, the formation contains double n; уби́тый has t. The retained source shows these forms from perfective verbs. This lesson recognizes the supplied forms; these endings alone are not a complete productive formation rule for every verb. The retained short form напи́сан has a single n and lacks the long adjective ending shown in напи́санный. Long versus short form is different from the action meaning: both writing forms concern writing. These checks select the action meaning of a supplied form; they do not test production of all short-form gender and number endings.

Counts ending in zero or five through nine use genitive plural in the basic construction. The teen exception also uses genitive plural. Ten and sixteen therefore fit this pattern. пять часов — пять часов. двадцать один час — двадцать один час.
